title: Why Can Log Footage Look Noisier After Rec.709 Conversion?
description: Log footage can look noisier after Rec.709 conversion because the transform changes contrast and makes existing shadow noise easier to see.
direct: Log footage can look noisier after Rec.709 conversion because the transform changes contrast and makes existing shadow noise easier to see. Conversion does not establish that the source was clean, and a LUT is not a denoiser.

cards.choice.heading: Start with the decision
cards.choice.body: A flat Log preview compresses the visible contrast of a scene. Normalizing that preview can reveal weak shadows, compression artifacts or an unsuitable exposure. A mismatched camera transform can create additional problems, so check the source profile before diagnosing the recording.
sections.detail-0.heading: Look at motion too
sections.detail-0.body: Noise changes between frames; a still can exaggerate or hide how distracting it is. Inspect a dark, relatively uniform area and a moving subject. Do not copy exposure numbers from another camera: appropriate capture settings depend on the camera, profile and scene. Sony’s technical discussion illustrates why exposure and viewing transforms are separate decisions.
sections.detail-1.heading: What VideoFix contributes
sections.detail-1.body: Space Sheep Studio develops VideoFix for iPhone. Its current public version converts Apple ProRes Log to Rec.709 SDR H.264 MP4. This creates a standard-color delivery copy; it does not promise noise removal or recovery of unrecorded detail. The first three conversions are free. Judge the export in the actual destination before processing more clips.

related.related.label: Related practical guide
steps.step-1.text: Compare the same frame at the same display size. Avoid judging one zoomed screenshot against another player’s fitted preview.
steps.step-2.text: Confirm the camera’s Log curve and gamut. Check whether your editor has already normalized the footage before adding a LUT.
steps.step-3.text: For supported Apple ProRes Log footage, create a short Rec.709 copy with VideoFix and examine shadows during playback. Retain the source for any separate grading or noise-reduction work.
